# Task: fix a reported bug in `chessground`

## Bug report (verbatim from the project's issue tracker)
**eraseOnClick doesn't work as expected**

The shape on the board can be erased by either clicking - which deleted all shapes - or by redrawing the same shape - which deletes just that shape.

There is a property on chessground.state.drawable called eraseOnClick, which by name should enable or disable the functionality to erase all shapes when clicking. However, as shown by this line:

https://github.com/lichess-org/chessground/blob/aad96fd5f5c6f95168d894986f106ab1846c2205/src/drag.ts#L35

the `drawClear` function will executed regardless of the eraseOnClick setting if one clicks on an empty square or one having a piece different from the turn color.

Also, drawClear is not something that is exposed by chessground, so I can't even override it.

I would like to be able to disable the "erase on click" functionality somehow.

Thanks.

3. Add or update a regression test that fails before your fix and passes after.
4. Run the project's test suite and make it green. Do not modify or delete unrelated tests.
5. When done, summarize: root cause, the files you changed, how you verified it.
Do not ask me for permission between steps; proceed until the task is complete, then report.

Author: @Siderite

## Body

The shape on the board can be erased by either clicking - which deleted all shapes - or by redrawing the same shape - which deletes just that shape.

There is a property on chessground.state.drawable called eraseOnClick, which by name should enable or disable the functionality to erase all shapes when clicking. However, as shown by this line:

https://github.com/lichess-org/chessground/blob/aad96fd5f5c6f95168d894986f106ab1846c2205/src/drag.ts#L35

the `drawClear` function will executed regardless of the eraseOnClick setting if one clicks on an empty square or one having a piece different from the turn color.

content.thinking:
The issue is still open on upstream (as of the API snapshot date). In other words, there is no upstream fix to reference — I need to design the fix myself.

Current state of this repository (v10.1.1):
- `drawable.eraseOnMovablePieceClick` (default `true`): if true, clicking on a movable piece (of the turn color, not currently selected) also clears the drawing.
- Clicks on empty squares or pieces of non-turn color always clear the drawing (there's no way to disable this).

Content of the bug report: the user wants to be able to completely disable the "clear on click" behavior. The property name `eraseOnClick` suggests it controls "clear all shapes on click," but in reality it (now named `eraseOnMovablePieceClick`) only controls part of it.

Root cause: the clear logic in `drag.ts start()` unconditionally executes `drawClear` for clicks on empty squares / non-turn-color pieces, and there is no configuration option that can disable this.

Design options:

**Option A**: Introduce a top-level `drawable.eraseOnClick` (default `true`) that gates all clearing on click, and keep `eraseOnMovablePieceClick` as a more fine-grained option:

```ts
if (
  !previouslySelected &&
  s.drawable.enabled &&
  s.drawable.eraseOnClick &&
  (s.drawable.eraseOnMovablePieceClick || !piece || piece.color !== s.turnColor)
)
  drawClear(s);
```

Hmm, but this creates a subtle interaction: if `eraseOnClick: false` and `eraseOnMovablePieceClick: true`… does clicking a movable piece also not clear? With this gate structure, `eraseOnClick: false` means no clearing anywhere. The `eraseOnMovablePieceClick` sub-option only makes sense when `eraseOnClick` is true. This is consistent: eraseOnClick = master switch, eraseOnMovablePieceClick = extended case.

Hmm wait, but there's actually a cleaner way to think about this. Let me reconsider: perhaps the cleanest minimal fix is to make the existing semantics respect a new flag `eraseOnClick`:

- `eraseOnClick` (default true): clearing on click of empty square or immovable piece.
- `eraseOnMovablePieceClick` (default true): additionally clears on click of a movable piece.

Logic:

```ts
if (!previouslySelected && s.drawable.enabled) {
  const erasable =
    (s.drawable.eraseOnClick && (!piece || piece.color !== s.turnColor)) ||
    (s.drawable.eraseOnMovablePieceClick && piece && piece.color === s.turnColor);
  if (erasable) drawClear(s);
}
```

This is a full matrix: 4 cases (empty, opponent's piece, own piece, already selected). The current behavior becomes `eraseOnClick=true, eraseOnMovablePieceClick=true`.

Wait, current behavior for a selected piece: `!previouslySelected` gates everything, so clicking an already-selected piece doesn't clear. Preserved.

Let me verify the current behavior matrix (eraseOnMovablePieceClick = true by default):
- Clicking empty square: `!piece` → true → clear.
- Clicking opponent's piece (color !== turnColor): `piece.color !== s.turnColor` → true → clear.
- Clicking own (turn color) piece: `eraseOnMovablePieceClick || ...` → true (default) → clear. If the property is false → no clear.
- Clicking an already-selected piece: `previouslySelected` is truthy → no clear.

Proposed behavior:
- `eraseOnClick: true` (default): empty / non-turn-color → clear (current behavior).
- `eraseOnClick: false`: empty / non-turn-color → no clear. This is what the user wants.
- `eraseOnMovablePieceClick` is unchanged: controls clearing on own-piece clicks.

Default behavior unchanged → backward compatible. Fix is minimal: 1 boolean config option + default + 1-line condition.

Hmm, one subtle point: is `eraseOnClick` the right name? The user explicitly said "there is a property called eraseOnClick in chessground.state.drawable" — in old versions it existed, and its semantics were "also clear when clicking a movable piece" (see the commit cded4a2 "add drawable.eraseOnClick option - bump v3.6.4"). The rename to `eraseOnMovablePieceClick` was to make it more precise. Now, reintroducing `eraseOnClick` with the master-switch semantics is exactly what the issue is asking for: "by its name, it should enable or disable the functionality to clear all shapes on click."

The issue title is "eraseOnClick doesn't work as expected," and the user says the name suggests it should enable/disable clearing on click. So implementing `eraseOnClick` as a master switch for clearing on click directly satisfies the request. And it restores the API name the user was expecting (which was removed in the rename — the rename can actually be said to have made this issue worse by removing the master switch).

Wait, actually, let me reconsider once more. Another possible design: instead of a new option, flip the semantics so that `eraseOnMovablePieceClick` becomes the only clearing-on-click trigger, i.e., clicking empty squares never clears. This would change default behavior — a breaking change for Lichess which relies on the current default. Bad idea. Keep default behavior identical.

So Option A (master switch, default true) is the right call:
- Backward compatible: default behavior is unchanged.
- Satisfies the report: `chessground.state.drawable.eraseOnClick = false` disables clearing on click (on any square).

Implementation:

1. `src/draw.ts` — `Drawable` interface: add `eraseOnClick: boolean;`.
2. `src/config.ts` — `drawable?` config: add `eraseOnClick?: boolean;` with a comment.
3. `src/state.ts` — default value `eraseOnClick: true,`.
4. `src/drag.ts` — condition:

```ts
  if (
    !previouslySelected &&
    s.drawable.enabled &&
    (s.drawable.eraseOnClick && (!piece || piece.color !== s.turnColor) ||
      s.drawable.eraseOnMovablePieceClick && piece && piece.color === s.turnColor)
  )
    drawClear(s);
```

Hmm, this is hard to read. Alternative:

```ts
  if (
    !previouslySelected &&
    s.drawable.enabled &&
    ((s.drawable.eraseOnClick && (!piece || piece.color !== s.turnColor)) ||
      (s.drawable.eraseOnMovablePieceClick && piece && piece.color === s.turnColor))
  )
    drawClear(s);
```

Or the simpler gate form:

```ts
  if (
    !previouslySelected &&
    s.drawable.enabled &&
    (s.drawable.eraseOnClick && (s.drawable.eraseOnMovablePieceClick || !piece || piece.color !== s.turnColor))
  )
    drawClear(s);
```

Hmm, which one? With the gate form, `eraseOnClick: false` disables all clearing, including on movable pieces. In the full-matrix form, `eraseOnClick: false` + `eraseOnMovablePieceClick: true` still clears when clicking own pieces. Which semantics are more consistent?

"eraseOnClick: disable clearing on click functionality" — the user wants no clearing on click. The gate form matches that directly: one switch that disables the whole thing.

But the matrix form is more composable. Honestly, the gate form is simpler and matches the issue's request precisely. But hmm, let me think about which is more "correct" as an API.

`eraseOnClick`: "clears the drawing when the user clicks a square (default true)."
`eraseOnMovablePieceClick`: "if true, clicking on a (currently unselected) movable piece also clears the drawing."

With the gate form, setting `eraseOnClick: false, eraseOnMovablePieceClick: true` would not clear on own-piece clicks — the sub-option is ignored. A bit confusing, but the sub-option is described as "also clears" — the "also" implies the base is enabled. I think the gate form is fine and simplest: it's the master switch, and that's exactly what the issue asks for.

Hmm, actually, wait. Let me reconsider the matrix form again. The matrix form treats the two options as orthogonal, which is a cleaner API (no hidden interaction). The code is only slightly more complex. But the gate form is 1 added boolean to the existing expression — a more minimal diff.

The task says "keep changes minimal." Gate form wins:

```ts
  if (
    !previouslySelected &&
    s.drawable.enabled &&
    s.drawable.eraseOnClick &&
    (s.drawable.eraseOnMovablePieceClick || !piece || piece.color !== s.turnColor)
  )
    drawClear(s);
```

That's minimal and clear: `eraseOnClick` is the master switch, and `eraseOnMovablePieceClick` extends it to movable pieces.

Next, the documentation comment in config.ts. Current comment:

```ts
    // Clicking an empty square or immovable piece will clear the drawing regardless, but when this property is true,
    // clicking on a (currently unselected) movable piece will also clear the drawing.
    eraseOnMovablePieceClick?: boolean;
```

New comment:

```ts
    // Clicking an empty square or a piece not of the turn color will clear the drawing. Set to false to
    // disable the "erase on click" functionality entirely.
    eraseOnClick?: boolean;
    // When this property is true, clicking on a (currently unselected) movable piece will also clear the drawing.
    eraseOnMovablePieceClick?: boolean;
```

Order: put eraseOnClick first (master switch), then the finer-grained option.

Now — wait, I need to double-check: does anything else call drawClear on click? Let me search for other call sites of `drawClear` / `clear` from draw.ts. The earlier grep only showed drag.ts:37. Also `end()` in drag.ts — when a click (no drag) ends, is anything cleared there? Let me check drag end and the events for click handling. Also check whether draw.ts start() has any clearing when clicking an existing shape with the same brush (the "redraw the same shape to erase" behavior) — that's a separate behavior (the XOR erase), which the user isn't asking to change.

Let me read drag.ts end() and events.ts to make sure there's no other path that clears shapes on click.
